hints: Factor out $3^{-3}$ and write the expression as $\frac1{27}(1+2x/3)^{-3}$.
Apply the binomial expansion with index $-3$ through the square term, then multiply every coefficient by $1/27$.
walkthrough:
Factor out the constant $3$ from the base $(3 + 2x)$:
$$(3 + 2x)^{-3} = \left[3\left(1 + \dfrac{2}{3}x\right)\right]^{-3} = 3^{-3}\left(1 + \dfrac{2}{3}x\right)^{-3} = \dfrac{1}{27}\left(1 + \dfrac{2}{3}x\right)^{-3}$$

Apply the binomial series formula $(1 + u)^n = 1 + nu + \dfrac{n(n - 1)}{2!}u^2 + \cdots$ with $n = -3$ and $u = \dfrac{2}{3}x$:
$$\text{Term in } x: (-3)\left(\dfrac{2}{3}x\right) = -2x$$
$$\text{Term in } x^2: \dfrac{(-3)(-4)}{2!}\left(\dfrac{2}{3}x\right)^2 = \dfrac{12}{2}\left(\dfrac{4}{9}x^2\right) = 6\left(\dfrac{4}{9}x^2\right) = \dfrac{24}{9}x^2 = \dfrac{8}{3}x^2$$

Combine the unsimplified terms inside the expansion:
$$\left(1 + \dfrac{2}{3}x\right)^{-3} = 1 - 2x + \dfrac{8}{3}x^2 + \cdots$$

Multiply every term by the outer scalar $\dfrac{1}{27}$ and simplify the coefficients:
$$(3 + 2x)^{-3} = \dfrac{1}{27}\left(1 - 2x + \dfrac{8}{3}x^2 + \cdots\right)$$
$$= \dfrac{1}{27}(1) - \dfrac{1}{27}(2x) + \dfrac{1}{27}\left(\dfrac{8}{3}x^2\right) + \cdots$$
$$= \dfrac{1}{27} - \dfrac{2}{27}x + \dfrac{8}{81}x^2 + \cdots$$
